item.title: French Polynesia Cabin Cruise: The Floating Boutique Hotel for Effortless Island Hopping
item.description: Imagine waking up in a comfortable suite aboard a premium catamaran. You stretch out on crisp sheets and wonder what spectacular view is awaiting you today. Will it be the majestic twin peaks of Bora Bora or the white sand beaches and tropical jungles of Huahine? You step on deck and sniff the air: today’s port is actually the vanilla-scented shores of Taha’a. That’s what life is like aboard a French Polynesia cabin cruise. Every day, you get to go on a new adventure. At night, you rest and relax in the comfort of a spacious cabin aboard a shared catamaran charter. For many travelers, the freedom to visit multiple destinations rather than be confined to a single resort makes a cabin cruise a much better option than a typical holiday on land. What Is a French Polynesia Cabin Cruise? A French Polynesia catamaran cruise or cabin cruise is a travel option where you book a private cabin with its own attached bathroom on a catamaran. Instead of chartering an entire yacht yourself, you share the vessel with a small group of other travelers. How Cabin Cruises Work The catamaran operates much like a small-scale cruise ship but with a personalized touch. Your captain navigates the islands, and an onboard steward prepares your meals. This vacation style eliminates the stress of trip planning, sailing logistics, and meal preparation. And since vessels are shared among travelers, cabin cruises are more affordable than booking Tahiti yacht charters . Why It Feels Like a Floating Boutique Hotel Unlike massive cruise ships that carry thousands of passengers, a catamaran hosts between 8 and 12 guests. This creates an intimate atmosphere, similar to that of a small hotel, except you also get to experience different destinations and activities every day. In French Polynesia, our cabin cruises are offered on the Bali 5.4, Lagoon 620, and the Fountaine Pajot Ipanema 58, each accommodating 12 guests. Comfort and Convenience: What Is a Cabin Cruise Like Onboard? Life aboard a cabin charter is defined by relaxation and comfort. Your catamaran features decks, shaded outdoor dining areas, and a forward trampoline net. This net is a great spot to lounge as the islands glide by. No jostling for sunbathing space on crowded beaches or lining up to rent gear from stands along the shore. You can get all the sun you want on deck, and the cruise includes the use of water sports equipment. You can step directly off the yacht’s transom steps into the water, swim, snorkel, or kayak to your heart’s content. Island Hopping Without Repacking or Airport Transfers With 118 islands and atolls spread across an area as vast as Western Europe, French Polynesia island hopping is all about discovering the unique character of each destination. However, having your base camp be a hotel or resort limits your options. It also means you have to go through a drawn-out process of getting there before you can visit each different island. Traditional travelers must pack their suitcases, check out of their resorts, take a taxi to the airport, wait in security lines, and fly to the next island, only to repeat the check-in process. Meanwhile, on Tahiti cabin cruises , you unpack your bags once on arrival. While you relax on deck or sleep in your cabin, the catamaran moves you between Tahiti and other destinations like Huahine, Raiatea, Taha’a, and Bora Bora. A Tahiti cabin charter eliminates the need for regional flights and ferry schedules, saving you both travel stress and vacation time. Space, Food, Privacy, and Seasickness: Honest Answers Before booking a sailing trip, it is normal to have a few questions about how things work on a boat. Here is what daily life aboard your shared luxury catamaran looks like. Space: Yacht cabins are smaller than hotel rooms, but they’re just as well-appointed. They feature built-in storage and ensuite bathrooms, with air-conditioning at specified daylight hours when you want a break from the tropical heat. Food: Your steward handles all the grocery …

item.title: Why The Bali 5.4 Should be Your Next Charter
item.description: The Bali 5.4 brings together space, comfort, and performance all in an impeccably designed 54-foot catamaran perfect for charter vacations. This yacht was built with a focus on open bright living spaces, comfortable accommodations, and plentiful outdoor spaces. With room for up to 12 in its six-cabin configuration, the Bali 5.4 is perfect for social sailing. Dream Yacht guests have the option to enjoy this yacht through a cabin cruise or when the yacht has availability outside of cabin charters, book it as a crewed yacht charter for an exclusive experience with family and friends. A Layout Designed for Living The center of the Bali 5.4’s design was built around bringing people together while still allowing space to spread out. Fluid flowing spaces from bow to stern creates seamless connection between the outdoor living areas, saloon, and aft cockpit. One of the most distinctive and innovative features of this yacht is the large pivoting rear door. It excellently connects the salon with the aft cockpit creating one extended living area and allowing for a larger conversation space. Another unique feature is the sliding windows that allow for more airflow and light giving an open air feel throughout. Forward of the saloon a door provides easy access to the foredeck. Here cushioned seats stretch out into the sun allowing guests to relax and enjoy the views while underway. While the aft cockpit provides a perfect gathering space for lunch or dinner at anchor with comfortable seating. The davits and swim ladder on the stern provide an easy access to the water for swimming. Then above there is a flybridge with a large U shaped seating area perfect for sipping a morning coffee with the sunrise or sundowners after a rewarding day of cruising. Forward of the seating area find the sunbathing pads where guests can lounge while taking in the breathtaking scenery of one of Dream Yacht’s incredible destinations. This Bali 5.4 provides so many areas where connection to the natural world and each other become possible. Find peace and shared experiences through innovation and exploration aboard this yacht. Take the Tour Comfortable Accommodations Below Deck The Bali 5.4 continues to deliver through its focus on comfort as we move below deck. Each cabin is equipped with queen sized beds, a private bathroom with a shower, and adequate storage space. Natural light and airflow are still features even down in the cabins; some cabins even have direct access to the deck. For large groups this layout is meant to give everyone their own private space at night, while relishing the communal spaces during the day. Guests get the feeling of home and settling in through these comfortable areas instead of the fleeting feeling of a hotel room. Why Charter the Bali 5.4 Space for Everyone – Roughly 130 square meters of living space allows for plenty of room to dine, relax, and enjoy cruising without feeling crowded. Indoor/Outdoor Living – The yacht’s flow from bow to stern and one of a kind opening door from the saloon to the aft cabin makes it easy to roam between the interior and exterior living spaces. Enjoy the breeze blowing through the yacht which creates a light airy open feel that connects you to the natural beauty of the surrounding world. Relaxation Area Options – There is no shortage of lounging areas onboard from the flybridge to the foredeck choose your ideal spot to enjoy the sail from. Now Newly Available for Private Crewed Charters When a Bali 5.4 is not being used on a cabin charter it will be available for a private crewed charter experience with a captain and hostess. This means families or groups of friends can experience the entire yacht privately, with a professional crew taking care of the sailing, itinerary, food, and day to day operation. Allowing guests to concentrate on relaxation and taking in the scenery from any of the comfortable lounging areas. item.title: Meet the Couple Behind Our BVI Crewed Catamaran Allende
item.description: Husband and wife duo, captain Graham Gips and chef Kristiann Gips are in their third season of operating crewed charters in the BVIs on board their yacht Allende, and they don’t do anything halfway. They started sailing a decade ago, while living in Lagos, Nigeria. After racing dinghies and competing internationally, they decided to honor their love of sailing and their passion for hosting guests by running their own charter yacht. We caught up with Kristiann to find out more about Allende , what they offer their customers and why they love their full-time sailing jobs. Life before sailing We used to have very normal lives working in the oil and gas industry. We consider ourselves lucky to have had jobs that sent us traveling internationally, but we secretly craved a life that was more serendipitous. We learned to sail together and now both hold a Master’s 50-ton license from the United States Coast Guard and are CPR/first aid certified. What a typical day looks like Graham spends most of his time sailing the boat, while I keep busy by creating bold-flavored dishes using what is available on and around the island. We also have a huge support staff on shore who help make it all happen, such as people who deliver provisions, to people who clean the boat, for example. What we love about our job Running our own business, working together and having control over the choices you make are the greatest rewards. But that is also the greatest challenge. We are solely responsible for our financial success. It is a very physical job – we love it but it takes a great amount of physical effort on a daily basis. Where our guests love to sail Our guests tend to ask to see The Baths and the Soggy Dollar Bar, but there are certain highlights that are favorites. For guests, we like to find anchorages where we are the only boat. Our crewed yacht is rented by one person for a family vacation or group of friends. The average size tends to be six people and we’ve looked after a huge variety of guests. We see lots of families with young and older kids who are celebrating special occasions, such as milestone anniversaries and birthdays. Why our vacations are so special Listening to what guests are saying and what they aren’t saying is our unique selling point. We make it seamless as an experience – from the moment they land, everything is arranged. Our itineraries work in the same way as our menus, they change depending on diet and preference. Nothing is preset. We work closely with our guests to tailor their vacation entirely to their liking. If you’re new to sailing, we’d love to teach you how much fun it can be. We also have special entertainment on board – our dog, Friday! Allende is a Fountaine Pajot Helia 44 Evolution crewed catamaran with three cabins that can accommodate six passengers sailing between October and August in the Caribbean. Learn More: Get in touch with DYC to book an all-inclusive, luxury crewed charter with Kristiann, Graham and Friday! item.title: Chartering A Power Catamaran With Dream Yacht Charter
item.description: Back in May we announced the exciting addition of power catamarans to our fleet, starting with initial availability in the British Virgin Islands , La Paz , and the Bahamas . But what do these FP Maestro 37ft yachts offer in terms of pros? We’ve put together the key benefits of how power catamarans offer a whole new experience for our charterers. Top power catamaran benefits Speed: It goes without saying that motor yachts tend to be a lot faster than sail yachts. Motor yachts like the FP Maestro 37 can hit up to 22 knots or so, depending on the sea conditions, which gives a great sense of freedom for thrill seekers. Sail yachts hit around 9-10 knots and are completely reliant on sea and wind conditions, plus the skills of the crew Efficiency: The extra 10 knots you have on a motor yacht means you can make the most of your vacation time. You can cover distances in half the time it takes a sail yacht, making motor yachts the perfect choice for island hopping and going short distances. This is why we featured motor yachts at our most popular island hopping and line of sight sailing destinations, so you can have more time exploring favourite islands or discovering new locations Clearance: Motor yachts also have low clearance, which means they are ideal for going under low bridges Relaxation: Their lack of a mast also makes motor yachts a perfect grab n’ go charter boat, as you won’t have to worry about raising or lowering sails. This means you won’t have to call your guests to be all hands on deck, but can focus on relaxing and letting the motor do the work Accessible: You can charter motor catamarans with just power boat experience on your bareboat resume. This means they are a great way for someone who may want to charter in international waters but have yet to gain sailing experience. If you don’t have any sailing or power boat experience, we can also book a professional captain to handle the vessel for you Our team is here to answer any questions to share current charter pricing and availability of our new lineup of FP Maestro 37s, just call our office at 855-650-8902 or email us .
